title: Electrically Conductive Scaffold to Modulate and Deliver Stem Cells
protocol: Place a masking agent over the conductive side of ITO-covered glass slide.
Remove excess mask, leaving only the desired shape of the final ITO design covered on the glass.
Combine 5% (v/v) of nitric acid and 45% (v/v) of HCl in a glass beaker inside a fume hood to prepare the etching solution.
Maintain temperature of etching solution at 70 °C using a hot plate and thermometer.
Place masked-ITO glass slide into the etching solution for 2 minutes.
Remove the slide from the etching solution and rinse it with deionized (DI) H2O.
Carefully remove the mask and measure resistance using a multimeter to ensure that the remaining ITO is intact.
Dissolve 70 g of sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (NaDBS) in 600 mL of DI H2O in a 1000 mL glass bottle.
Add 14 mL of 0.2 M pyrrole to the NaDBS solution.
Add 386 mL of DI H2O to the solution.
Cover the solution with aluminum foil and store at 4°C.
Warm the pyrrole solution to room temperature until NaDBS is fully redissolved.
Pour 25 mL of the pyrrole solution into a beaker.
Connect the etched ITO glass to a multimeter and submerge the slide into the pyrrole solution.
Ensure that the side with 0 Ω resistance is facing towards the platinum mesh reference electrode.
Apply an electrical current to initiate electroplating of PPy on the ITO surface using a multimeter (current controlled at 3 mA/cm² for 4 hours).
Remove the ITO glass from the multimeter and wash electroplated-PPy in DI H2O to remove residual surfactant.
Gently detach the electroplated-PPy plate from the ITO glass using a razor blade.
Store the PPy plate at room temperature.
Mix 18 g of base agent with 2 g of curing agent and pour the mixture into two 10 cm x 8 cm glass molds.
Remove the bubbles from the molds using a vacuum chamber for 15 - 20 minutes.
Place the molds in a 70 °C oven for 3 h.
Once cooled, use a flat spatula to remove the PDMS from the molds.
Autoclave the metal plates (WxL, 2.5 cm x 12.5 cm) and flow valves at 120°C for 1 hour.
Using a chamber slide as a template, cut two pieces of PDMS.
Cut out the inside cell chamber so that it is square shaped and matches the shape of the cell chamber.
Layer the materials as following from bottom to top: Metal plate, PDMS (without cutouts), PPy plate, PDMS (with cutouts), and cell chamber.
Clamp the apparatus together once it is fully aligned.
Cut two 60 cm pieces of a metal wire and attach one wire to each end of the PPy plate using silver paste.
Ensure that the wires are long enough to extend from the apparatus to the outside of an incubator.
Record the resistance using a multimeter to make sure that the applied field is the same in each chamber.
Remove the wires for implantation.
Unclamp the cell chambers and PDMS and separate them from the conductive scaffold.
Sterilize the assembled chambers under UV light for 2 hours.
Rotate the assembled chambers 90° after 1 hour.
Sterilize the chamber.
Coat the surface of PPy in the bottom of the chamber with 800 µL of coating substrate.
Incubate the coated chamber at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Remove the supernatant from the chambers after 1 hour.
Gently rinse the chambers with 1 mL of DPBS + Ca + Mg per well.
Mechanically dissociate cultured cells using fresh cell media by gentle pipetting.
Collect hNPC pellets through centrifugation at 8000 x g for 5 minutes.
Count and resuspend the cells at a volume corresponding to 100,000 cells/cm².
Plate 100,000 cells into each chamber well with 1 mL of media.
Return the chambers to the incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
One day after seeding, remove old media from each chamber well.
Replenish each chamber well with 800 µL of fresh media.
Place the chambers back into the incubator and extend wires out of the incubator.
Attach the extended wires to a waveform generator.
Apply electrical stimulation to the cells using a square wave signal at ±400 mV with 100 Hz for 1 hour.
Remove the wires after stimulation.
Incubate the chambers for another day at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Perform cell viability analysis as per manufacturer's protocol.
Conduct qRT-PCR analysis according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Induce anesthesia in adult male nude rats using isoflurane via inhalation.
Confirm anesthetization by absence of toe pinch reflex response.
Monitor rat’s membrane color, breathing pattern, and rectal temperature every 15 minutes during surgery.
Apply artificial tears on the eyes of the anesthetized rat to prevent dryness.
Maintain aseptic technique by wearing sterile gloves and using a sterile surgical drape.
Keep all surgical instruments within a sterile field.
Drill a craniectomy above the left cortex while the rat is under anesthesia.
Open the dura mater.
Remove the dura mater from the brain using a micro-thin surgical needle.
Implant conductive scaffolds onto the rat cortex.
Implant scaffolds on the penumbral cortex medial to the stroke lesion.
Place surgicel over the implant to prevent movement during skin closure.
Suture the wound shut.
Subcutaneously inject rats with buprenorphine SR at 1 mg/kg for pain management.

Monitor animals daily for signs of pain including body weight loss, decreased food/water intake, reduced grooming/unkempt coat, abnormal posture, dehydration/skin tenting, sunken eyes, hiding, self-mutilation, rapid breathing, open mouthed breathing, twitching, trembling, tremor, and vocalization.
Monitor animals daily until they are eating, drinking, grooming, and gaining weight.
Continue monitoring weekly after the animal starts to gain weight.
Euthanize animals via CO2 inhalation if they show signs of not eating, drinking, or gaining weight after surgery.
Confirm euthanasia by ensuring the animal does not revive when normal oxygen supply is restored.
Euthanize animals if they appear to be in pain after the initial surgical procedure.
Euthanize animals if they are unable to complete behavioral tests due to a larger motor cortex deficit.
